name: Question 14
problem:
Consider the following initial value problem for the functions $y=y(x),z=z(x),w=w(x):$

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}=y+z+w,\, & y(0)=1 \\ {z}^{′}=xy-{w}^{2},\, & z(0)=-2 \\ {w}^{′}=\frac{yz}{w},\, & w(0)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Use Euler's Method with one step to approximate $y\,(\frac{1}{2}),$ $z\,(\frac{1}{2}),$ and $w\,(\frac{1}{2}).$

$\,y\,(\frac{1}{2})≈$
{{field-1}},
$\,z\,(\frac{1}{2})≈$
{{field-2}},
$\,w\,(\frac{1}{2})≈$
{{field-3}}
worked_solution:
Euler's method approximates the solution of an initial value problem containing a system of ODEs by applying the update rule component-wise to each equation.

Since we want to find the values of $y,$ $z,$ and $w$ at $x=\frac{1}{2},$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=\frac{1}{2}-0=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

First, we place the initial condition data in a table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ |  |  | $-2$ |  |  | $1$ |  |  |

Next, we compute ${y}^{′},$ ${z}^{′},$ and ${w}^{′}$ according to the given rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y+z+w \\  & =1+(-2)+1 \\  & =0 \\ {z}^{′} & =xy-{w}^{2} \\  & =0\cdot 1-{1}^{2} \\  & =-1 \\ {w}^{′} & =\frac{yz}{w} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (-2)}{1} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add these to our table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $0$ |  | $-2$ | $-1$ |  | $1$ | $-2$ |  |

Next, we compute $Δy,$ $Δz,$ and $Δw$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =0\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =0 \\ Δz & ={z}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(-1)\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2} \\ Δw & ={w}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(-2)\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

We add these to our table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $0$ | $0$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $-\frac{1}{2}$ | $1$ | $-2$ | $-1$ |

To get the new values of $x,$ $y,$ $z,$ and $w$ in the *next* row, we add $Δx$ to $x,$ $Δy$ to $y,$ $Δz$ to $z,$ and $Δw$ to $w,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=0+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy=1+0=1 \\ {z}_{\text{new}} & =z+Δz=-2+(-\frac{1}{2})=-\frac{5}{2} \\ {w}_{\text{new}} & =w+Δw=1+(-1)=0\end{aligned}
$$

Adding these values to our table in a new row gives the following:

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $0$ | $0$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $-\frac{1}{2}$ | $1$ | $-2$ | $-1$ |
| $\frac{1}{2}$ | $1$ |  |  | $-\frac{5}{2}$ |  |  | $0$ |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
y\,(\frac{1}{2})≈1,\,z\,(\frac{1}{2})≈-\frac{5}{2},\,w\,(\frac{1}{2})≈0.
$$
